relevance_note: Cohort of 31 suspected Behçet's disease patients in which five individually described cases had HA20: "Five patients (cases 5, 10, 14, 29, 31) were classified as having Haploinsufficiency of A20 (HA20)".
method_note: Read the full paper and supplement by hand; a short Python script assembled the JSON from my readings and sliced Table 1 row text for spans (output checked against the table). Scope: the five HA20 cases (cases 5, 10, 14, 29, 31) plus relatives described in relation to them; the other 26 cohort members (BD, ISG15, CVID, TRAPS) get no rows. Labels follow rule 1 because the text calls the Table 1 'Case' numbers 'case 5', 'Case 29' etc. Case 29's 'maternal cousins' (number not stated) were given no rows; the statement 'Mother, but not other mildly affected relatives, also found to have TNFAIP3: p.C657Vfs*14 mutation' is ambiguous about whether the other relatives were tested negative, so no variant rows or test results were recorded for the grandmother or brother. 'Similar features in mother' (case 10) and 'similar symptoms' (relatives of case 29) name no specific feature, so no feature rows were made for those relatives. Case 10 has two TNFAIP3 rows in Table 1 (946G>A/G316S and 1625_1626insGAC TACAGCAGAGGCC/S548Dfs*128); the text lists only p.S548Dfs*128 among the five HA20 variants; both recorded. Nucleotide changes are printed without a 'c.' prefix and recorded as printed; the transcript is described only as the HGNC RefSeq transcript, with no accession, so transcript is not reported. Contradictions: Table 1 gives variant classification 3 (Class 3: unknown significance) for all TNFAIP3 variants, while the Discussion says six of the seven novel proposed disease-causing variants are pathogenic by ACMG and only case 5's p.T76I remains a VUS; I recorded the per-row table value (plus the VUS sentence for case 5). The main text says the NF-kB assay showed upregulation in all four tested cases (5, 14, 29, 31), whereas Supplementary Fig. S1 says case 29 showed less activation (attributed to treatment); both quoted for case 29. Case 14: the table says 'chronic pulmonary interstitial emphysema' and the text 'chronic interstitial pneumonia'; both recorded as features, interstitial lung disease checklist marked observed from the text. Checklist judgements: perianal ulcers/fistula (case 31) and colitis (case 29) counted as gastrointestinal inflammation; livedo reticularis (case 29) counted as a skin lesion; 'redness of the eyes' (case 5) not counted as ocular inflammation; tonsilitis/recurrent tonsilitis not counted as recurrent infections (the paper does not call it infectious); headaches not counted as CNS involvement; autoimmune hypothyroidism counted as autoimmune thyroiditis. Age column is 'Age at the time of this study' (recorded as age at last evaluation). Table 1 footnote a (family DNA used for segregation) applies to cases 5 and 14 but gives no parental result, so parental testing is not reported for them. No phenotypic exclusions were recorded: the paper reports no explicit absences for the HA20 cases. Variant classes (missense, frameshift) are not stated by the authors and were not derived from HGVS.
